findings.title: Late confirmed game is stranded by one-time worker snapshot and unique KEEP scheduling
findings.trigger: Confirm B while W already downloaded its candidates snapshot containing A; A then finishes successfully with no retry path.
reproducer: Confirm A and let W pass TransferWorker.kt:L35 with candidates=[A].
Confirm a different B while A downloads. B commits; KEEP encounters running W and does not insert a successor.
Let every candidate in W's original snapshot complete successfully.
W returns success; B remains run/queued with no executor until another scheduling action.
findings.consequence: Normal second-game download can wait indefinitely after first completes; refreshing a page/catalogue does not schedule it.
compensatingControls: A retry from another candidate or explicit later scheduling action may discover B.
limitations: Static deduction; no executed Android test.
Requires an all-success original snapshot; errors may mask it by causing retry.
findings.correction: Make enqueue/drain completion race-safe and persist a successor or continuously drain all runnable committed tasks.

findings.title: Stale full-row worker Upsert revives cancellation after a replacement task is created
findings.trigger: Cancel and replace an established active task between worker checkpoint read and full-row progress Upsert.
reproducer: For established multi-chunk A with stored state downloading, hold worker after L139 reads intent=run and before L140 commits.
Cancel A. transferAction persists cancel/cancelled; old downloading state means no immediate directory deletion.
Return to detail and confirm replacement B. UI and enqueue both exclude cancelled A, so B commits.
Allow stale worker L140 Upsert. It restores A intent=run/state=downloading. A and B are both active for the same game.
findings.consequence: Cancellation is lost and duplicate same-game active operations/copies are admitted; A continues unwanted work.
compensatingControls: Unique WorkManager work still serializes actual game transfers.
Installation operationLock serializes extraction; A/B task roots differ.
Normal detail UI treats failed as existing; merely excluding failed in enqueue is not by itself a routine UI reproducer.
limitations: No claim of simultaneous network connections or simultaneous extraction.
Race derived from source and suspend/commit interleaving; not executed on Android.
findings.correction: Use conditional state/progress updates preserving current intent, retain cancellation ownership until executor acknowledgement, and enforce one active operation per game in DB and coordinator.

findings.title: Queue does not apply task-ID tie-break and UI displays reverse history without positions
findings.trigger: Equal created timestamps, or ordinary A-then-B confirmation while reviewing the download list.
reproducer: Have two queued records with equal created and opposite insertion/task-ID order; no SQL/coordinator tie-break forces required task-ID order.
Confirm B after active A; UI reverses created-order list and renders B above A without a queue position or reverse-history explanation.
findings.consequence: Execution order is unspecified for ties and users cannot read the effective FIFO order from the displayed list.
limitations: No data loss or concurrency outcome established.
Source-only ordering/display check; timestamp tie not exercised.
findings.correction: Persist stable confirmation order, sort by it and task ID, and display effective queue position/reason.
